questions.stem: Thistlefen raises the price of its specialty coffee while costs stay constant. Assuming demand is unchanged, what happens to its break-even quantity?

options.text: It increases because higher prices always raise costs
options.misconception: Assumes costs rise with price without cause

options.text: It doubles because price and break-even are proportional
options.misconception: Confuses a higher margin with a fixed multiple

options.text: It decreases because contribution per unit is larger
It stays the same because only volume matters
options.misconception: Ignores that price changes contribution per unit

questions.explanation: A higher price increases contribution per unit when costs are constant, so fewer units are needed to cover fixed costs and break-even quantity falls. Price does not by itself raise costs, and the relationship is not a fixed multiple.
questions.hint: Higher margin per unit means fewer units needed.
